Tasks and resourceConstraints.

| Code | Severity | Summary | Python |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`bad_resource_constraint`](#bad_resource_constraint) | error | A resource constraint has an empty task name. | no |
| [`duplicate_constraint`](#duplicate_constraint) | warning | Two resource constraints name the same task. | no |
| [`bad_max_concurrent`](#bad_max_concurrent) | error | A resource constraint's maxConcurrent is not an integer >= 1. (not reachable today) | no |
| [`task_not_constrained`](#task_not_constrained) | error, warning | A task used by steps has no resource constraint. | no |
| [`unused_constraint`](#unused_constraint) | warning | A resource constraint names a task no step uses. | no |

### `bad_resource_constraint` {#bad_resource_constraint}

**Error.** A resource constraint has an empty task name.

Each entry of resourceConstraints limits one task type. A missing task is a schema_required finding; an empty string is reported here.

**Example.** Merged over the [base program](#base-program):

```json
{ "resourceConstraints": [{ "task": "", "maxConcurrent": 1 }] }
```

**Fix.** Set task to the task name the steps use, or remove the entry.

**Python.** Python reports nothing for it.

### `duplicate_constraint` {#duplicate_constraint}

**Warning.** Two resource constraints name the same task.

Only one limit can apply to a task; which one wins depends on the reader.

**Example.** Merged over the [base program](#base-program):

```json
{
  "tracks": [
    {
      "trackId": "main",
      "name": "Main",
      "steps": [
        {
          "stepId": "prep",
          "name": "Prep",
          "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 300 },
          "startTrigger": { "type": "programStart" },
          "task": "oven"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "resourceConstraints": [
    { "task": "oven", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "oven", "maxConcurrent": 2 }
  ]
}
```

**Fix.** Keep one constraint per task.

**Python.** Python reports nothing for it.

### `bad_max_concurrent` {#bad_max_concurrent}

**Error.** A resource constraint's maxConcurrent is not an integer >= 1.

Meant for a maxConcurrent below 1 or not a number.

!!! note "Not reachable today"
    The schema requires maxConcurrent to be an integer >= 1 and reports it (schema_required, schema_type, schema_minimum); this check stays quiet wherever the schema has spoken. Dead code in validateProgram.

**Fix.** Set maxConcurrent to a whole number of at least 1.

**Python.** Python reports nothing for it.

### `task_not_constrained` {#task_not_constrained}

**Error or Warning.** A task used by steps has no resource constraint.

Every task named by a step (task, tasks, taskResources, buffer taskResources) needs an entry in resourceConstraints, so the runner knows how many can run at once. It is an error, unless the program names an environment or actors, which may supply the constraint: then it is a warning.

**Example 1 (error).** Merged over the [base program](#base-program):

```json
{
  "tracks": [
    {
      "trackId": "main",
      "name": "Main",
      "steps": [
        {
          "stepId": "prep",
          "name": "Prep",
          "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 300 },
          "startTrigger": { "type": "programStart" },
          "task": "oven"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

**Example 2 (warning).** Merged over the [base program](#base-program):

```json
{
  "tracks": [
    {
      "trackId": "main",
      "name": "Main",
      "steps": [
        {
          "stepId": "prep",
          "name": "Prep",
          "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 300 },
          "startTrigger": { "type": "programStart" },
          "task": "oven"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "actors": 2
}
```

**Fix.** Add {"task": "<task>", "maxConcurrent": N} to resourceConstraints.

**Python.** Python reports nothing for it. Python checks it only with --strict (strict=True), as an error, whatever the program names.

### `unused_constraint` {#unused_constraint}

**Warning.** A resource constraint names a task no step uses.

Usually a typo in the task name on the constraint or on the steps.

**Example.** Merged over the [base program](#base-program):

```json
{ "resourceConstraints": [{ "task": "oven", "maxConcurrent": 1 }] }
```

**Fix.** Remove the constraint, or set task on the steps that use it.

**Python.** Python reports nothing for it.

## Instances and replicates {#instances}

Schema 0.3.0-alpha `instances` triggers, `replicates` and maxInFlight, and replicate expansion.

| Code | Severity | Summary | Python |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`E_INSTANCES_ON_SINGLE`](#E_INSTANCES_ON_SINGLE) | error | `instances` is used on a reference to a step that is not replicated. | `E_INSTANCES_ON_SINGLE` |
| [`E_EACH_WITH_REPLICATES`](#E_EACH_WITH_REPLICATES) | error | A step has both an instances: "each" trigger and its own `replicates`. | `E_EACH_WITH_REPLICATES` |
| [`E_EACH_COUNT_MISMATCH`](#E_EACH_COUNT_MISMATCH) | error | A compound "each" trigger pairs groups of different sizes. | `E_EACH_COUNT_MISMATCH` |
| [`E_INFLIGHT_GT_COUNT`](#E_INFLIGHT_GT_COUNT) | error | replicates.maxInFlight is greater than replicates.count. | `E_INFLIGHT_GT_COUNT` |
| [`E_INFLIGHT_NO_CHAIN`](#E_INFLIGHT_NO_CHAIN) | error | maxInFlight on a serial replicate with no "each" descendants has no effect. | `E_INFLIGHT_NO_CHAIN` |
| [`W_UNBARRIERED_CHAIN`](#W_UNBARRIERED_CHAIN) | warning | An instances: "each" chain has no "all" barrier, but later steps do not wait for it. | `W_UNBARRIERED_CHAIN` |
| [`I_IMPLICIT_BARRIER`](#I_IMPLICIT_BARRIER) | info | A 0.3.0 program waits for a replicated step without saying `instances`. | no |
| [`expansion_failed`](#expansion_failed) | error | Replicates could not be expanded. | none (CLI), `expansion_failed` (library) |

### `E_INSTANCES_ON_SINGLE` {#E_INSTANCES_ON_SINGLE}

**Error.** `instances` is used on a reference to a step that is not replicated.

`instances` ("each", "all", "any") says how a reference fans in over a replicated step's copies. The referenced step has no `replicates` and is not itself per-instance, so there is nothing to fan in.

**Example.** Merged over the [base program](#base-program):

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": "0.3.0-alpha",
  "tracks": [
    {
      "trackId": "main",
      "name": "Main",
      "steps": [
        {
          "stepId": "mix",
          "name": "Mix",
          "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 300 },
          "startTrigger": { "type": "programStart" }
        },
        {
          "stepId": "cool",
          "name": "Cool",
          "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 300 },
          "startTrigger": { "type": "afterStep", "stepId": "mix", "instances": "each" }
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

**Fix.** Remove `instances`, or add `replicates` to the referenced step.

**Python.** Python reports `E_INSTANCES_ON_SINGLE`.

### `E_EACH_WITH_REPLICATES` {#E_EACH_WITH_REPLICATES}

**Error.** A step has both an instances: "each" trigger and its own `replicates`.

instances: "each" already makes one copy of the step per upstream instance; its own `replicates` would multiply them again.

**Example.** Merged over the [base program](#base-program):

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": "0.3.0-alpha",
  "tracks": [
    {
      "trackId": "main",
      "name": "Main",
      "steps": [
        {
          "stepId": "mix",
          "name": "Mix",
          "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 300 },
          "startTrigger": { "type": "programStart" }
        },
        {
          "stepId": "bake",
          "name": "Bake",
          "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 300 },
          "startTrigger": { "type": "afterStep", "stepId": "mix" },
          "replicates": { "count": 3 }
        },
        {
          "stepId": "cool",
          "name": "Cool",
          "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 300 },
          "startTrigger": { "type": "afterStep", "stepId": "bake", "instances": "each" },
          "replicates": { "count": 2 }
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

**Fix.** Drop `replicates` on the step; it inherits the upstream count.

**Python.** Python reports `E_EACH_WITH_REPLICATES`.

### `E_EACH_COUNT_MISMATCH` {#E_EACH_COUNT_MISMATCH}

**Error.** A compound "each" trigger pairs groups of different sizes.

Instance i of the step pairs with instance i of every "each" upstream, so all of them need the same count.

**Example.** Merged over the [base program](#base-program):

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": "0.3.0-alpha",
  "tracks": [
    {
      "trackId": "sauce",
      "name": "Sauce",
      "steps": [
        {
          "stepId": "sauce",
          "name": "Sauce",
          "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 300 },
          "startTrigger": { "type": "programStart" },
          "replicates": { "count": 2 }
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "trackId": "pasta",
      "name": "Pasta",
      "steps": [
        {
          "stepId": "pasta",
          "name": "Pasta",
          "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 300 },
          "startTrigger": { "type": "programStart" },
          "replicates": { "count": 3 }
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "trackId": "plating",
      "name": "Plating",
      "steps": [
        {
          "stepId": "plate",
          "name": "Plate",
          "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 300 },
          "startTrigger": {
            "logic": "all",
            "triggers": [
              { "type": "afterStep", "stepId": "sauce", "instances": "each" },
              { "type": "afterStep", "stepId": "pasta", "instances": "each" }
            ]
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

**Fix.** Give the upstream steps the same replicates.count.

**Python.** Python reports `E_EACH_COUNT_MISMATCH`.

### `E_INFLIGHT_GT_COUNT` {#E_INFLIGHT_GT_COUNT}

**Error.** replicates.maxInFlight is greater than replicates.count.

maxInFlight caps how many instances are in progress at once; it cannot exceed the number of instances.

**Example.** Merged over the [base program](#base-program):

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": "0.3.0-alpha",
  "tracks": [
    {
      "trackId": "main",
      "name": "Main",
      "steps": [
        {
          "stepId": "mix",
          "name": "Mix",
          "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 300 },
          "startTrigger": { "type": "programStart" }
        },
        {
          "stepId": "bake",
          "name": "Bake",
          "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 300 },
          "startTrigger": { "type": "afterStep", "stepId": "mix" },
          "replicates": { "count": 3, "maxInFlight": 5 }
        },
        {
          "stepId": "cool",
          "name": "Cool",
          "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 300 },
          "startTrigger": { "type": "afterStep", "stepId": "bake", "instances": "each" }
        },
        {
          "stepId": "box",
          "name": "Box",
          "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 300 },
          "startTrigger": { "type": "afterStep", "stepId": "cool", "instances": "all" }
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

**Fix.** Set maxInFlight to at most count, or omit it.

**Python.** Python reports `E_INFLIGHT_GT_COUNT`.

### `E_INFLIGHT_NO_CHAIN` {#E_INFLIGHT_NO_CHAIN}

**Error.** maxInFlight on a serial replicate with no "each" descendants has no effect.

Serial instances never overlap, and with no per-instance steps after them an instance is done as soon as it ends, so the cap never holds one back.

**Example.** Merged over the [base program](#base-program):

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": "0.3.0-alpha",
  "tracks": [
    {
      "trackId": "main",
      "name": "Main",
      "steps": [
        {
          "stepId": "mix",
          "name": "Mix",
          "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 300 },
          "startTrigger": { "type": "programStart" }
        },
        {
          "stepId": "bake",
          "name": "Bake",
          "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 300 },
          "startTrigger": { "type": "afterStep", "stepId": "mix" },
          "replicates": { "count": 3, "mode": "serial", "maxInFlight": 2 }
        },
        {
          "stepId": "box",
          "name": "Box",
          "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 300 },
          "startTrigger": { "type": "afterStep", "stepId": "bake", "instances": "all" }
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

**Fix.** Remove maxInFlight, or chain a per-instance step after it with instances: "each".

**Python.** Python reports `E_INFLIGHT_NO_CHAIN`.

### `W_UNBARRIERED_CHAIN` {#W_UNBARRIERED_CHAIN}

**Warning.** An instances: "each" chain has no "all" barrier, but later steps do not wait for it.

The per-instance chain is never joined, so nothing waits for every instance to finish while other work carries on. Often a missing barrier step.

**Example.** Merged over the [base program](#base-program):

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": "0.3.0-alpha",
  "tracks": [
    {
      "trackId": "cookies",
      "name": "Cookies",
      "steps": [
        {
          "stepId": "mix",
          "name": "Mix",
          "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 300 },
          "startTrigger": { "type": "programStart" }
        },
        {
          "stepId": "bake",
          "name": "Bake",
          "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 300 },
          "startTrigger": { "type": "afterStep", "stepId": "mix" },
          "replicates": { "count": 3, "mode": "serial" }
        },
        {
          "stepId": "cool",
          "name": "Cool",
          "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 300 },
          "startTrigger": { "type": "afterStep", "stepId": "bake", "instances": "each" }
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "trackId": "cleanup",
      "name": "Cleanup",
      "steps": [
        {
          "stepId": "wipe",
          "name": "Wipe",
          "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 300 },
          "startTrigger": { "type": "programStartOffset", "offsetSeconds": 3600 }
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

**Fix.** Add a step with instances: "all" on the chain's last step if later work should wait for every instance.

**Python.** Python reports `W_UNBARRIERED_CHAIN`.

### `I_IMPLICIT_BARRIER` {#I_IMPLICIT_BARRIER}

**Info.** A 0.3.0 program waits for a replicated step without saying `instances`.

A reference to a replicated step with no `instances` waits for every instance (an implicit "all" barrier), as in 0.2.0. In 0.3.0-alpha programs the note suggests saying so.

**Example.** Merged over the [base program](#base-program):

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": "0.3.0-alpha",
  "tracks": [
    {
      "trackId": "main",
      "name": "Main",
      "steps": [
        {
          "stepId": "mix",
          "name": "Mix",
          "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 300 },
          "startTrigger": { "type": "programStart" }
        },
        {
          "stepId": "bake",
          "name": "Bake",
          "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 300 },
          "startTrigger": { "type": "afterStep", "stepId": "mix" },
          "replicates": { "count": 3, "mode": "serial" }
        },
        {
          "stepId": "box",
          "name": "Box",
          "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 300 },
          "startTrigger": { "type": "afterStep", "stepId": "bake" }
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

**Fix.** Add instances: "all" to make the barrier explicit, or "each" to run the step once per instance.

**Python.** Python reports nothing for it. JS only (PRD per-instance triggers §9 Q5).

### `expansion_failed` {#expansion_failed}

**Error.** Replicates could not be expanded.

The replicate expander rejected the program; the message says why. The one case the checks before it do not catch: instances: "all" or "any" inside a compound trigger of the other logic, which would need a nested compound. The program is then schema-checked as written.

**Example.** Merged over the [base program](#base-program):

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": "0.3.0-alpha",
  "tracks": [
    {
      "trackId": "main",
      "name": "Main",
      "steps": [
        {
          "stepId": "bake",
          "name": "Bake",
          "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 300 },
          "startTrigger": { "type": "programStart" },
          "replicates": { "count": 2 }
        },
        {
          "stepId": "box",
          "name": "Box",
          "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 300 },
          "startTrigger": {
            "logic": "all",
            "triggers": [
              { "type": "afterStep", "stepId": "bake", "instances": "any" },
              { "type": "programStart" }
            ]
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

**Fix.** Check `replicates` and `instances` on the steps the message names; match the compound's logic to `instances` or split the trigger.

**Python.** `rhylthyme validate` reports nothing; `validate_program_structured` reports `expansion_failed`. `rhylthyme validate` does not expand replicates, so it has nothing to fail; validate_program_structured does.

## Alerts {#alerts}

Step alerts (offsets before or after a step's start or end).

| Code | Severity | Summary | Python |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`E_ALERT_BAD_OFFSET`](#E_ALERT_BAD_OFFSET) | error | An alert's offsetSeconds is not a number or time string. | `E_ALERT_BAD_OFFSET` |
| [`W_ALERT_BEFORE_MANUAL_START`](#W_ALERT_BEFORE_MANUAL_START) | warning | An alert before the start of a manually started step never fires. | `W_ALERT_BEFORE_MANUAL_START` |
| [`W_ALERT_BEFORE_PROGRAM_START`](#W_ALERT_BEFORE_PROGRAM_START) | warning | An alert would fire before the program starts, so it never fires. | `W_ALERT_BEFORE_PROGRAM_START` |
| [`W_ALERT_BEFORE_INDEFINITE_END`](#W_ALERT_BEFORE_INDEFINITE_END) | warning | An alert before the end of an indefinite step never fires. | `W_ALERT_BEFORE_INDEFINITE_END` |

### `E_ALERT_BAD_OFFSET` {#E_ALERT_BAD_OFFSET}

**Error.** An alert's offsetSeconds is not a number or time string.

offsetSeconds is signed seconds or a signed time string ("-2m", "30s", "1h30m") relative to the step's start or end.

**Example.** Merged over the [base program](#base-program):

```json
{
  "tracks": [
    {
      "trackId": "main",
      "name": "Main",
      "steps": [
        {
          "stepId": "prep",
          "name": "Prep",
          "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 300 },
          "startTrigger": { "type": "programStart" },
          "alerts": [{ "event": "end", "offsetSeconds": "a bit before" }]
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

**Fix.** Use seconds (-120) or a signed time string ("-2m").

**Python.** Python reports `E_ALERT_BAD_OFFSET`.

### `W_ALERT_BEFORE_MANUAL_START` {#W_ALERT_BEFORE_MANUAL_START}

**Warning.** An alert before the start of a manually started step never fires.

A manual step's start is not known until someone starts it, so an alert timed before it has no anchor.

**Example.** Merged over the [base program](#base-program):

```json
{
  "tracks": [
    {
      "trackId": "main",
      "name": "Main",
      "steps": [
        {
          "stepId": "prep",
          "name": "Prep",
          "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 300 },
          "startTrigger": { "type": "manual" },
          "alerts": [{ "event": "start", "offsetSeconds": "-1m" }]
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

**Fix.** Anchor the alert on the end of the step before, or use offsetSeconds >= 0.

**Python.** Python reports `W_ALERT_BEFORE_MANUAL_START`.

### `W_ALERT_BEFORE_PROGRAM_START` {#W_ALERT_BEFORE_PROGRAM_START}

**Warning.** An alert would fire before the program starts, so it never fires.

The step starts at (or soon after) the program start and the alert's negative offset reaches further back than that.

**Example.** Merged over the [base program](#base-program):

```json
{
  "tracks": [
    {
      "trackId": "main",
      "name": "Main",
      "steps": [
        {
          "stepId": "prep",
          "name": "Prep",
          "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 300 },
          "startTrigger": { "type": "programStart" },
          "alerts": [{ "event": "start", "offsetSeconds": -300 }]
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

**Fix.** Shorten the offset, or delay the step with programStartOffset.

**Python.** Python reports `W_ALERT_BEFORE_PROGRAM_START`.

### `W_ALERT_BEFORE_INDEFINITE_END` {#W_ALERT_BEFORE_INDEFINITE_END}

**Warning.** An alert before the end of an indefinite step never fires.

An indefinite step has no projected end, so an alert timed before it has no anchor.

**Example.** Merged over the [base program](#base-program):

```json
{
  "tracks": [
    {
      "trackId": "main",
      "name": "Main",
      "steps": [
        {
          "stepId": "prep",
          "name": "Prep",
          "duration": { "type": "indefinite", "defaultSeconds": 900 },
          "startTrigger": { "type": "programStart" },
          "alerts": [{ "event": "end", "offsetSeconds": "-2m" }]
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

**Fix.** Use offsetSeconds >= 0 on event "end", or give the step a fixed or variable duration.

**Python.** Python reports `W_ALERT_BEFORE_INDEFINITE_END`.

## Instruments {#instruments}

Instrument steps: galago-tools commands and LabMCP server calls.

| Code | Severity | Summary | Python |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`I_INSTRUMENT_DURATION`](#I_INSTRUMENT_DURATION) | info | An instrument step with no duration ends when its call replies; timings use an estimate. | no |
| [`instrument_bad_shape`](#instrument_bad_shape) | error | A step's instrument block is malformed. | `schema_error` |
| [`instrument_no_end`](#instrument_no_end) | warning | An instrument step has no command, no until and no duration: only the operator can end it. | `instrument_no_end` (CLI), none (library) |
| [`instrument_unchecked`](#instrument_unchecked) | warning | Instrument calls were not checked. | `instrument_unchecked` (CLI), none (library) |
| [`instrument_unknown_tool_type`](#instrument_unknown_tool_type) | error, warning | An instrument's toolType is not a known galago tool type or LabMCP server. | `instrument_unknown_tool_type` (CLI), `logic_error` (library) |
| [`instrument_invalid_command`](#instrument_invalid_command) | error | An instrument call is not valid for its tool type. | `instrument_invalid_command` (CLI), `logic_error` (library) |
| [`instrument_over_limit`](#instrument_over_limit) | error | A LabMCP call's parameter is beyond the server's default limit. | `instrument_over_limit` (CLI), `logic_error` (library) |
| [`instrument_returns_early`](#instrument_returns_early) | error | A LabMCP call that replies as soon as it starts is used to end a step. | `instrument_returns_early` (CLI), `logic_error` (library) |
| [`instrument_dose_outlasts_step`](#instrument_dose_outlasts_step) | warning | A pump dose started by a step takes longer than the step. | `instrument_dose_outlasts_step` (CLI), none (library) |
| [`instrument_catalog_not_loaded`](#instrument_catalog_not_loaded) | warning | A LabMCP step was not checked because the LabMCP catalogue is not loaded. | no |

### `I_INSTRUMENT_DURATION` {#I_INSTRUMENT_DURATION}

**Info.** An instrument step with no duration ends when its call replies; timings use an estimate.

The step's command (or until call) ends it, so it needs no duration. For planning, the validator and analyzer time it by an estimate from its params (e.g. a shake's duration, a LabMCP series' count x interval) or a default, and say which.

**Example.** Merged over the [base program](#base-program):

```json
{
  "tracks": [
    {
      "trackId": "main",
      "name": "Main",
      "steps": [
        {
          "stepId": "shake",
          "name": "Shake",
          "startTrigger": { "type": "programStart" },
          "instrument": {
            "tool": "shaker",
            "toolType": "bioshake",
            "command": "start_shake",
            "params": { "speed": 1000, "duration": 300 }
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

**Fix.** Nothing to fix. `rhylthyme plan --workcell` writes the tool's own estimate into the program.

**Python.** Python reports nothing for it.

### `instrument_bad_shape` {#instrument_bad_shape}

**Error.** A step's instrument block is malformed.

The instrument has a missing or empty tool, both command and until, no call or actions at all, an empty start/end/onAbort list, an action without a command, an unknown key or a bad timeoutSeconds. The schema reports the same problem (schema_*), with the program path; this finding says it in the instrument's own terms. The step's calls are not checked further.

**Example.** Merged over the [base program](#base-program):

```json
{
  "tracks": [
    {
      "trackId": "main",
      "name": "Main",
      "steps": [
        {
          "stepId": "shake",
          "name": "Shake",
          "startTrigger": { "type": "programStart" },
          "instrument": {
            "tool": "shaker",
            "toolType": "bioshake",
            "command": "start_shake",
            "params": { "speed": 1000, "duration": 300 },
            "start": []
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Also emits schema_minItems.

**Fix.** Use {"tool": "shaker", "command": "start_shake", "params": {...}}, or start/until/end actions: {"command", "params", "tool"}.

**Python.** Python reports `schema_error`. Python reports a malformed instrument through its schema check only.

### `instrument_no_end` {#instrument_no_end}

**Warning.** An instrument step has no command, no until and no duration: only the operator can end it.

Its start actions run and nothing ends the step on its own. Timings use a default.

**Example.** Merged over the [base program](#base-program):

```json
{
  "tracks": [
    {
      "trackId": "main",
      "name": "Main",
      "steps": [
        {
          "stepId": "shake",
          "name": "Shake",
          "startTrigger": { "type": "programStart" },
          "instrument": {
            "tool": "shaker",
            "toolType": "bioshake",
            "start": [
              { "command": "start_shake", "params": { "speed": 1000, "duration": 300 } }
            ]
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

**Fix.** Add a duration, or an until action whose reply ends the step.

**Python.** `rhylthyme validate` reports `instrument_no_end`; `validate_program_structured` reports nothing. validate_program_structured keeps only the errors of the instrument checks.

### `instrument_unchecked` {#instrument_unchecked}

**Warning.** Instrument calls were not checked.

The step's instrument has no toolType, or some of its actions go to another tool, so the commands cannot be checked without the lab's workcell file.

**Example.** Merged over the [base program](#base-program):

```json
{
  "tracks": [
    {
      "trackId": "main",
      "name": "Main",
      "steps": [
        {
          "stepId": "shake",
          "name": "Shake",
          "startTrigger": { "type": "programStart" },
          "instrument": {
            "tool": "shaker",
            "command": "start_shake",
            "params": { "speed": 1000, "duration": 300 }
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

**Fix.** Add toolType (the galago tool type, e.g. "bioshake", or a LabMCP package such as "labmcp-ika"), or run `rhylthyme validate --workcell`.

**Python.** `rhylthyme validate` reports `instrument_unchecked`; `validate_program_structured` reports nothing. Python reports it once per program ("Instrument steps were not checked") when the driver package is missing, and as an error with --workcell. validate_program_structured keeps only the errors of the instrument checks.

### `instrument_unknown_tool_type` {#instrument_unknown_tool_type}

**Error or Warning.** An instrument's toolType is not a known galago tool type or LabMCP server.

An unknown galago toolType is an error. A toolType starting with "labmcp-" that is not in the LabMCP catalogue is a warning: the server may be newer than the catalogue, so its calls are just not checked.

**Example 1 (error).** Merged over the [base program](#base-program):

```json
{
  "tracks": [
    {
      "trackId": "main",
      "name": "Main",
      "steps": [
        {
          "stepId": "shake",
          "name": "Shake",
          "startTrigger": { "type": "programStart" },
          "instrument": {
            "tool": "shaker",
            "toolType": "blender",
            "command": "start_shake"
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

**Example 2 (warning).** Merged over the [base program](#base-program):

```json
{
  "tracks": [
    {
      "trackId": "main",
      "name": "Main",
      "steps": [
        {
          "stepId": "heat",
          "name": "Heat",
          "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 300 },
          "startTrigger": { "type": "programStart" },
          "instrument": {
            "tool": "stirrer",
            "toolType": "labmcp-nope",
            "command": "stop_heating"
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

**Fix.** Use a galago tool type the message lists, or a LabMCP package name from the catalogue.

**Python.** `rhylthyme validate` reports `instrument_unknown_tool_type`; `validate_program_structured` reports `logic_error`. Needs `rhylthyme-galago` / `rhylthyme-labmcp`. validate_program_structured keeps only the errors of the instrument checks, as logic_error.

### `instrument_invalid_command` {#instrument_invalid_command}

**Error.** An instrument call is not valid for its tool type.

The command does not exist for the toolType, or its params do not match the command's parameters (unknown, missing or of the wrong type). galago tool types are checked against galago-tools' commands, LabMCP servers against the LabMCP catalogue.

**Example.** Merged over the [base program](#base-program):

```json
{
  "tracks": [
    {
      "trackId": "main",
      "name": "Main",
      "steps": [
        {
          "stepId": "shake",
          "name": "Shake",
          "startTrigger": { "type": "programStart" },
          "instrument": {
            "tool": "shaker",
            "toolType": "bioshake",
            "command": "start_shake",
            "params": { "rpm": 1000 }
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

**Fix.** Use a command and params the message lists for that tool type.

**Python.** `rhylthyme validate` reports `instrument_invalid_command`; `validate_program_structured` reports `logic_error`. Needs `rhylthyme-galago`. From the rhylthyme-galago / rhylthyme-labmcp driver packages, when installed. validate_program_structured reports it as logic_error.

### `instrument_over_limit` {#instrument_over_limit}

**Error.** A LabMCP call's parameter is beyond the server's default limit.

LabMCP servers refuse values past their safety limits (a maximum temperature, a series length, ...). The check uses each server's default limits; a lab may configure others.

**Example.** Merged over the [base program](#base-program):

```json
{
  "tracks": [
    {
      "trackId": "main",
      "name": "Main",
      "steps": [
        {
          "stepId": "heat",
          "name": "Heat",
          "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 300 },
          "startTrigger": { "type": "programStart" },
          "instrument": {
            "tool": "stirrer",
            "toolType": "labmcp-ika",
            "start": [
              { "command": "set_temperature", "params": { "temperature_c": 200 } }
            ]
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

**Fix.** Use a value within the limit the message names, or raise the limit in the server's configuration.

**Python.** `rhylthyme validate` reports `instrument_over_limit`; `validate_program_structured` reports `logic_error`. Needs `rhylthyme-labmcp`. From rhylthyme-labmcp, when installed. validate_program_structured reports it as logic_error.

### `instrument_returns_early` {#instrument_returns_early}

**Error.** A LabMCP call that replies as soon as it starts is used to end a step.

Some calls (a syringe pump's infuse and withdraw) reply when the work starts, not when it is done; as the step's command or until call they would end the step at once.

**Example.** Merged over the [base program](#base-program):

```json
{
  "tracks": [
    {
      "trackId": "main",
      "name": "Main",
      "steps": [
        {
          "stepId": "dose",
          "name": "Dose",
          "startTrigger": { "type": "programStart" },
          "instrument": {
            "tool": "pump",
            "toolType": "labmcp-new-era",
            "command": "infuse",
            "params": { "volume_ml": 1, "rate_ml_min": 1 }
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

**Fix.** Send it as a start action and give the step a duration at least as long as the dose.

**Python.** `rhylthyme validate` reports `instrument_returns_early`; `validate_program_structured` reports `logic_error`. Needs `rhylthyme-labmcp`. From rhylthyme-labmcp, when installed. validate_program_structured reports it as logic_error.

### `instrument_dose_outlasts_step` {#instrument_dose_outlasts_step}

**Warning.** A pump dose started by a step takes longer than the step.

The dose's volume / rate is longer than the step's duration, so its end actions and the next steps start while the pump still runs.

**Example.** Merged over the [base program](#base-program):

```json
{
  "tracks": [
    {
      "trackId": "main",
      "name": "Main",
      "steps": [
        {
          "stepId": "dose",
          "name": "Dose",
          "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 10 },
          "startTrigger": { "type": "programStart" },
          "instrument": {
            "tool": "pump",
            "toolType": "labmcp-new-era",
            "start": [
              { "command": "infuse", "params": { "volume_ml": 1, "rate_ml_min": 1 } }
            ]
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

**Fix.** Lengthen the step to at least the dose time, or lower the volume or raise the rate.

**Python.** `rhylthyme validate` reports `instrument_dose_outlasts_step`; `validate_program_structured` reports nothing. Needs `rhylthyme-labmcp`. From rhylthyme-labmcp, when installed. validate_program_structured keeps only the errors of the instrument checks.

### `instrument_catalog_not_loaded` {#instrument_catalog_not_loaded}

**Warning.** A LabMCP step was not checked because the LabMCP catalogue is not loaded.

The browser entry of @rhylthyme/timeline/schedule (and browser/schedule.js) leaves out the LabMCP catalogue (about 350 KB). Until it is registered, each LabMCP step gets this warning instead of its checks. The Node entry always has it.

**Example.** Merged over the [base program](#base-program):

```json
{
  "tracks": [
    {
      "trackId": "main",
      "name": "Main",
      "steps": [
        {
          "stepId": "heat",
          "name": "Heat",
          "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 300 },
          "startTrigger": { "type": "programStart" },
          "instrument": {
            "tool": "stirrer",
            "toolType": "labmcp-ika",
            "start": [
              { "command": "set_temperature", "params": { "temperature_c": 40 } }
            ]
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Validated with the browser entry before the LabMCP catalogue is registered.

**Fix.** import '@rhylthyme/timeline/schedule/labmcp-catalog' (or add browser/labmcp-catalog.js to the page) before validating.

**Python.** Python reports nothing for it. Python always has its catalogue.
